land.text: the Ottoman Sanjak of Montenegro: "In 1514, Zeta was separated from the Sanjak of Scutari and established as the separate Sanjak of Montenegro" under Skenderbeg Crnojević (to 1528)

predecessors.note: "Vavila was elected as ruler of Montenegro by its clans" in 1516, two years after the sanjak was made; the page does not say the sanjak ended.

land.text: the secular Principality of Montenegro: Danilo "turned his land into a secular principality" in 1852

successors.note: Infobox: secularised 13 March 1852; Cliopatria's Montenegro row starts in 1853 with 6,131 km2.

capitals.name: Cetinje
capitals.note: Infobox capital: Cetinje; the page calls the rulers Metropolitans of Cetinje.

correction.text: Old Montenegro, the clans round Cetinje that elected Vavila in 1516

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria's Montenegro row begins in 1853. The page names no boundary: the infobox map labels "Old Montenegro" and the hill tribes only as map notes. The 30 km circle round Cetinje (about 1,500-2,000 km2 on the cell grid) is the researcher's reading. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: the 30 km circle round Cetinje no longer takes in the Bay of Kotor and the Budva coast (Kotor, Tivat, Budva, Herceg Novi), which the first version drew as Montenegrin from 1516; the bay was Venetian to 1797 and Austrian from 1815, and Montenegrin only in 1813-1814]

correction.text: Old Montenegro with the Bjelopavlići and the Piperi, joined after the victory of 1796

keyframe_review.note: Petar I page: "The Montenegrin victory resulted in territorial expansion," with the Bjelopavlići and Piperi joining the state, then "Black Mountain (Montenegro) and the Hills". Danilovgrad municipality stands for the Bjelopavlići and the 25 km circle (19.1 E, 42.65 N) for the Piperi, both the researcher's reading. The keyframe is about 2,800 km2 on the cell grid; Cliopatria's 1853 shape is 6,131 km2 (shapes.csv; 5,564 km2 on the same grid), a ratio of 0.5, so the keyframe leaves out the other tribes that joined by 1853, whose dates no page opened gives. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: the 30 km circle round Cetinje no longer takes in the Bay of Kotor and the Budva coast (Kotor, Tivat, Budva, Herceg Novi), which the first version drew as Montenegrin from 1516; the bay was Venetian to 1797 and Austrian from 1815, and Montenegrin only in 1813-1814]

correction.text: with the Bay of Kotor: "in 1813, a union of the bay area with Montenegro was declared"

keyframe_review.note: Bay of Kotor page for 1813; the main page: Montenegrin forces with Russian and British support liberated the bay from the French. The page is silent on whether Montenegro held Herceg Novi, Budva or Risan in 1814.

correction.text: the Bay of Kotor lost: "In 1815, the bay was annexed by the Austrian Empire"

keyframe_review.note: Bay of Kotor page. The Petar I page adds that in 1828-29 "recognition of Montenegrin sovereignty over Piperi" followed the repulse of an Ottoman invasion from Albania. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: the 30 km circle round Cetinje no longer takes in the Bay of Kotor and the Budva coast (Kotor, Tivat, Budva, Herceg Novi), which the first version drew as Montenegrin from 1516; the bay was Venetian to 1797 and Austrian from 1815, and Montenegrin only in 1813-1814]

region.text: Montenegro, where "Vavila was elected as ruler of Montenegro by its clans"

ledger.note: 1516: the clans elect Vavila prince-bishop, founding the Prince-Bishopric (the page: "prince-bishops of Cetinje ruled from 1516 until 1852"). The Ottomans had made the Sanjak of Montenegro in 1514; the page gives no boundary for the new rule. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: region no longer includes the Bay of Kotor and the Budva coast]

1767: the Prince-Bishopric is "temporarily abolished in 1767-1773" when the impostor Šćepan Mali "posed as the Russian Emperor" and the Montenegrins accepted him as emperor (1766-1768); the metropolitans return in 1773. No land changes.

region.text: Old Montenegro: in June 1785 Kara Mahmud Pasha of Scutari "attacked Montenegro"

ledger.note: 1785: Kara Mahmud attacks Montenegro, "crossing Bjelice before withdrawing" (Petar I page); the Scutari pashalik's own page says he "conquered it in just four days".
1789: "The Ottoman Porte formally recognized Montenegro's independence under Petar I" (main page; the Petar I page dates a Russian subsidy to 1799). No land changes.

region.text: the Bjelopavlići and the Piperi, who "joined the state" after the victory

ledger.note: 22 September 1796: Petar I defeats Kara Mahmud at Krusi (after Martinići): "The Montenegrin victory resulted in territorial expansion". The Hills were officially joined under Petar I; the page gives no separate date. The pashalik-of-scutari dossier carries the matching 1796 loss with the same region. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: counterpart loss now exists]
22 September 1796: Kara Mahmud is killed at Krusi and his army defeated; Montenegro keeps its mountains.

region.text: the Bay of Kotor: "Montenegrin forces, with Russian battalions and Admiral Senyavin's fleet, drove French troops back toward Dubrovnik and besieged it"

ledger.note: 1806: war over the Bay of Kotor, which the Treaty of Pressburg (1805) had set to pass from Habsburg to French rule (Bay page).
1807: "The Treaty of Tilsit gave control of the Bay of Kotor to France"; Petar I's plan to unite the Bay, Herzegovina, Dubrovnik and Dalmatia is thwarted.

region.text: the Bay of Kotor: "in 1813, a union of the bay area with Montenegro was declared"

ledger.note: 1813: Montenegrins with Russian and British support free the Bay of Kotor from the French and declare its union with Montenegro.
1815: "the bay was annexed by the Austrian Empire" and joined to the province of Dalmatia.

region.text: the whole of the Prince-Bishopric, now a secular principality

ledger.note: 13 March 1852: Danilo renounces his ecclesiastical character, takes the title of knjaz and turns the Prince-Bishopric into the secular Principality of Montenegro.

wars.name: War of Cyprus
wars.outcome: Montenegrins fought for Venice under Pahomije; no change of Montenegro's land recorded.

wars.name: War of Candia
wars.outcome: Montenegrins fought on Venice's side; no change of land recorded.

wars.name: Morean War
wars.outcome: Montenegrins fought, including at the 1687 Battle of Herceg Novi; no change of Montenegro's own land recorded.

wars.name: Kara Mahmud Bushati's campaigns against Montenegro
wars.outcome: Defeat in June 1785; victories at Martinići (July) and Krusi (22 September 1796) in which Kara Mahmud was killed; the Bjelopavlići and Piperi joined Montenegro.

wars.name: Montenegrin-Russian war with France over the Bay of Kotor
wars.outcome: The Bay passed to France at Tilsit (1807), was freed and united with Montenegro in 1813, and was annexed by Austria in 1815.
wars.note: The pages give no month for the 1813 liberation.

certainty.note: Tribal territories with no surveyed frontier; the 1813 Bay of Kotor union and the 1796 Hills are approximate. The Ottoman frontier was not delimited on any page opened.

notes: Cliopatria has no row before 1853; all four keyframes are new and approximate (a 30 km circle round Cetinje for Old Montenegro). Gaps: the dates at which the Moračani, Rovčani, Kuči, Nikšić area and other tribes joined (Cliopatria's 1853 shape is 6,131 km2, the keyframes here about 2,800 km2); the pages say only that 1819-1820 brought a "successful campaign against the Bosnia Eyalet" and a battle won by the Moračani. The ruler list on the main page runs only to Arsenije Plamenac (1781-1784) and the infobox adds Ivan Vukotić (1831-1834), Pero Petrović (1834-1852) and Danilo II (1851-1852), so the ruler strip is omitted rather than guessed; Petar I (chosen 1781) and Petar II have no reign years on the pages opened. Disagreement: the Bay page says Montenegro and Russia held the bay "later" without dates; the Bay of Kotor 1806-1807 control of Montenegro is not dated by any page, hence contest events not gains. Venice paid haraç to Kara Mahmud (Scutari page). Counterpart slugs russian-empire and first-french-empire follow polities.csv. Wikidata id null (unreachable). Review fix (2026-11-01): the circle round Cetinje (18.92 E, 42.39 N, 30 km) is now taken minus the Kotor, Tivat, Budva and Herceg Novi municipalities in every keyframe, the found region, the contest zones and the predecessor land; 3 of its 7 cells had been Venetian (1420-1797) and then Austrian coast. The 1813-1814 keyframe adds the bay back explicitly. The 1796 gain of the Bjelopavlići and Piperi now has its matching loss in pashalik-of-scutari. The ruler strip (Petar I 1784-1830, Petar II 1830-1851) is still omitted: the pages opened give no reign years.
